 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. KANSAS CITY, Mo. — The NCAA has officially appealed a court ruling allowing Kansas men's basketball forward Trey Kaufman-Renn to play during the 2026-27 season.
 According to the Indiana Court of Appeals docket, the NCAA filed its notice of appeal Thursday, Nov. 5.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement  UMKC basketball kicks off season with Streetcar shuttle events  
 The appeal challenges an earlier ruling from a Clark County, Indiana, judge that granted Kaufman-Renn a preliminary injunction against the NCAA. That ruling allowed him to pursue another season of college basketball while his legal case against the organization continues.
 Kaufman-Renn transferred to Kansas after spending four seasons at Purdue. He is seeking a sixth-year of college eligibility after redshirting his first season due to a knee injury.
 Kaufman-Renn was selected 59th overall in the second round of the 2026 NBA Draft by the Minnesota Timberwolves, but ultimately chose to return to college after going unsigned on a guaranteed contract with the team.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kansas added Kaufman-Renn to its roster in October, and he made his regular-season debut with the Jayhawks against Fordham on Nov. 2.
 During that game, Kaufman-Renn made an efficient debut scoring nine points and grabbing five rebounds in 23-minutes off the bench, helping Kansas defeat Fordham 95-65.

 The NCAA's appeal marks another development in the legal battle over Kaufman-Renn's eligibility. The case remains pending before the Indiana Court of Appeals.
